# Project setup: choices and rationale

The project started with only an esbuild build script and a `tsconfig.json`. This document explains what was changed or added and why.

## `.gitignore`, and removing generated files from git

The initial commit included `node_modules/` (about 4,300 files), the `dist/` build output, macOS `.DS_Store` files and JetBrains `.idea/` settings because there was no `.gitignore` file in the project. A `.gitignore` has been added to exclude all of these. They were also removed from git's index to clean-up the repo.

- **`node_modules/`**: `package-lock.json` already pins every version, so `npm ci` restores exactly the same tree. Committing dependencies bloats the repo, makes diffs unreadable, and breaks packages that have platform-specific binaries. esbuild is one of those: the committed copy was built for macOS on Apple silicon only.
- **`dist/`**: this is the build output, and `npm start` always rebuilds it. A committed copy can only fall out of date. (That happened here: see the next section.)
- **`.idea/`, `.vscode/`, `.DS_Store`**: personal editor and OS files. The one useful project setting in `.idea/` was "use Prettier". That is now enforced for every editor by Prettier's config and the `format:check` script.
- It also ignores `coverage/`, logs, `.env*` files (so secrets aren't committed by accident) and tool caches.

`mock-service-worker/mockServiceWorker.js` stays committed on purpose. MSW recommends committing the generated worker script, and the build copies it into `dist/` from there.

## Mock Service Worker: serving the right worker version

MSW intercepts requests in the browser with a generated script, `mockServiceWorker.js`. Each MSW release ships its own version of that script, and the script must come from the same release as the MSW library bundled into `client.js`.

The repo had two copies of the script, and they didn't match:

- `framework/mock-server/mockServiceWorker.js` was generated by **MSW 2.3.1**. The build copied this file into `dist/`, so it was the one the browser received.
- `mockServer/mockServiceWorker.js` was generated by **MSW 2.15.0**. That's the installed version: `package.json` allows any 2.x release from 2.3.0 (`"msw": "^2.3.0"`), and `package-lock.json` pins **2.15.0**. `package.json` also named `mockServer` as MSW's `workerDirectory`, the folder MSW writes the worker into.

The browser was therefore running a 2.3.1 worker alongside the 2.15.0 MSW library code. The two versions exchange messages in different formats, so this can cause version-mismatch warnings or broken mocking in the browser.

**Fix:** a one-line change to the `build:server` script, which now copies the up-to-date worker from the `workerDirectory` instead of `framework/mock-server/`. The outdated 2.3.1 copy was deleted. Keeping the worker in its existing `workerDirectory` was the smallest change. MSW doesn't require a particular folder; its docs only say the worker must be served from the app's public URL root. Here the server does that by serving `dist/mockServiceWorker.js` at `/mockServiceWorker.js`.

**Folder rename:** `mockServer/` was then renamed to `mock-service-worker/`. It was the only camelCase folder in a repo that otherwise uses kebab-case (`caching-fetch-library/`, `framework/mock-server/`). Kebab-case is the common convention for JavaScript folder names, and all-lowercase names avoid case-sensitivity problems between macOS and Windows (case-insensitive by default) and Linux. The new name describes the folder's contents and avoids confusion with `framework/mock-server/`, which holds the request handlers. The `workerDirectory` setting, the build script, and the ESLint and Prettier ignore lists were updated to match.

## Type checking: TypeScript (`tsc --noEmit`)

esbuild removes types without checking them, and `typescript` wasn't installed, so the code was never actually type-checked. The brief requires `cachingFetch.ts` to pass a type check, so `typescript` is now a dev dependency and `npm run typecheck` runs it.

`tsconfig.json` was rewritten (the old one was mostly default comments) to describe how the code is really built:

- `"noEmit": true`: `tsc` only checks types. esbuild and Vitest handle the transpiling.
- `"module": "esnext"` and `"moduleResolution": "bundler"`: the code is bundled by esbuild, not run as CommonJS by Node. This is also what lets packages that use subpath exports, like `msw/browser` and `msw/node`, resolve correctly.
- `"isolatedModules": true`: esbuild compiles each file separately, so this flags TypeScript features that only work when compiling the whole program at once.
- `"strict": true` and `"jsx": "react"` are kept from the original. The JSX setting matches the existing `import React` style.
- `"include"` limits the check to source and test folders, so `dist/` and the generated worker are skipped.

TypeScript is pinned to `~6.0`. TypeScript 7 (the Go rewrite) is the current `latest`, but `typescript-eslint` only supports TypeScript up to 6.0.

## Linting: ESLint 9 with typescript-eslint and React rules

`eslint.config.mjs` uses ESLint's flat config format with:

- `@eslint/js` and `typescript-eslint` recommended rules, for common mistakes in JS and TS.
- `eslint-plugin-react`, for JSX mistakes such as missing `key` props.
- `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`, for the rules of hooks. These matter here because the main deliverable is a custom hook.
- `eslint-config-prettier`, which turns off style rules so ESLint and Prettier don't conflict. ESLint handles correctness and Prettier handles formatting.

Unused variables are **warnings**, not errors. The unfinished `cachingFetch.ts` has unused parameters, and it shouldn't fail the lint while work is in progress. Prefixing a name with `_` marks it as intentionally unused.

The setup uses ESLint 9 rather than 10 because `eslint-plugin-react` doesn't support ESLint 10 yet.

## Formatting: Prettier

`.prettierrc.json` sets `singleQuote` and `trailingComma: "all"`. Those choices match the existing code, so adopting Prettier changed almost nothing. `.prettierignore` excludes build output, the lockfile, the generated MSW worker (it should stay exactly as MSW ships it) and `DevTask.md` (kept exactly as provided).

## Unit tests: Vitest, Testing Library and jsdom

**Vitest** was chosen because it runs TypeScript and JSX with no extra setup, using the same esbuild-based transform as the build. Jest would need Babel or ts-jest. Tests run in Node by default; component tests switch to a **jsdom** browser environment with a `// @vitest-environment jsdom` comment. **React Testing Library** checks what users see instead of component internals.

Tests sit next to the code they cover (`*.test.ts(x)`). Shared fixtures live in `test/fixtures.ts`.

| Test file                               | What it covers                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `application/validation.test.ts`        | Valid data passes. Missing fields, wrong types and payloads that aren't arrays are rejected.                                                                                                            |
| `application/App.test.tsx`              | Loading, error and data states. Rendering through `Person` and `Name`. Invalid data throws. `preLoadServerData` preloads the right URL. The caching hook is stubbed, so these tests only cover the app. |
| `framework/server/buildHtmlDoc.test.ts` | The HTML shell: `#app` container, the optional client script, and `__INITIAL_DATA__` injection.                                                                                                         |
| `framework/server/renderApp.test.tsx`   | The SSR pipeline: preload, then serialize, then render; and that the client-only mode skips both steps.                                                                                                 |
| `framework/mock-server/handler.test.ts` | The MSW handler answers the real people URL with data that passes the app's validation. It also checks that the status is 202, not 200.                                                                 |

Not covered yet: `framework/server/index.ts` starts listening as soon as it's imported, so it can't be tested without refactoring it to export the server. `framework/client/index.tsx` needs a browser. The caching fetch library will get its own tests as part of Task 2.
